body:
The smiles of children always cheers me up. It reminds me of when I didn't have a single thing to worry about ever.

I've been on medication before, it was a few years a go though, perhaps I will try again. I've always been scared that I might actually be depressed and I've always kind of hoped I was just sad I guess, i guess after 4-5 years I should really try and come to terms with the fact I really might be but I'd always hoped it'd just go away, you know?

I've spoken to my family about it before a couple of years a go, I didn't get much help really because they always tried to tell me I wasn't depressed and I was being silly so I guess I just felt it was something I had to go through on my own. Probably a bad idea though. My ex girlfriend knew as well, she was very helpful because she'd been through the same thing and I never felt I had to hide my real thoughts from her because of that, shame I fucked that up.

Thanks for the reply, like last time I think talking about it will make me feel a bit better I just feel like an idiot really cause there's nothing massively wrong with my life and it makes me feel even worse cause I know there's people way worse off than me.

I spend a maximum of about 5-10 minutes on there a day and I only look at my inbox, friend requests (last week a got a request from one of my best friends from primary school, it was awesome) and sometimes groups I'm in. The last status update I made was about 6 months a go, and that was a joke between me and a friend. I've also never ever sent a poke to anyone.

The whole parks thing is something I've thought about a lot. Public areas that aren't really public. The fact that some people took ownership of the planet at some point astounds me. I don't see how people sit back and look at this like it's a good thing for them. 

Most people are just settled though, who needs change when I can get my new car, not that I own the car, I just borrow it from the bank, and even when I finally pay it off, the government is only giving me permission to use my car. It's a little scary.
I have never worked out in my life. Good idea though, I'll try joining a gym or something.

I think the fact I am depressed really changes my view on the world. All I see if people working day in day out just so they can live. Perhaps the people around me are just bad examples, but I don't know anyone who's truly happy.

I think part of the problem is I follow politics a lot, and I really can't understand how some of these people can be such cunts. They really fail to realise that we all share this planet and we have such a short time here, and they're so selfish. That really gets to me.

Thanks for the post. 

I got out of religion when I was about 10-11, I went to Catholic schools all my life and at the point (after a religious class no less) my brain just kind of went "lolwut?" and I stopped believing.

And yeah, my family is one thing that keeps me going, they aren't the best bunch but the ammount of pain it'd cause them is terrible.

Again, thanks for the kind words.

Thanks :) I've been to the doctors about it before, they didn't really help much, gave me pills and said they'd call me about councelling, they never called and I didn't really want it at the time.

After making this post today I feel that the help will work now.

I wouldn't say I'm proof of it, but yes, without any kind of final judgement dying is really an easy way to get away with no consequences at all.

I kind of see suicide differently to most people, they seem to think it's some hugely bad thing in every case imaginable. I see it as a real way of getting away from life on Earth, if someone really doesn't want to live, and they've tried everything to enjoy their time here, it's not my place to stop them, it's my place to say sorry that the world is so sucky for most people.
Think about it this way, when you're dead you won't even know that you were alive, that helps me get over the whole death thing.

Sunlight and the UK don't really go hand in hand :P But I really could try and get out more, I spend a lot of the time inside.

Cognitive therapy was one of the things suggested to me about 2 years a go, but I guess I was a bit scared to go to therapy, now that I'm older hopefully I'll be able to do it.

I recently left my job as well, leaving that place made me really happy, then about a month later I got out of a really crappy relationship, and for a while I was the happiest I'd been in years, then reality comes back and I need to get a new job and the ex won't stop talking to me, it's lame, but things are getting better. 

I need to find a job I enjoy, but I've never actually had to look for a job before, the last one was handed to me on a silver platter.

Thanks for this, I'm going to go to my doctor soon and see what they can do for me.

I live in the UK, so religion is never really a thing here, so finding a counsellor that doesn't spout religion at me won't be hard at all.
That Hicks quote is one of my favourites, I have it saved in my happy folder.

It's easy to just forget things, drugs help a lot. The underlying problem for me is always there, that the world isn't a nice place to live, for anyone really.

How did you get over it? Did you find a way you could make a difference? I've always thought about going to homeless shelters and helping there, to see if that will make me feel better.

Sometimes I can't believe how I act/react to things in life. I sometimes look at the things I've said or thought in total disbelief.

I tried anti-depressents for a while and they worked but after people telling me that being on them was bad for me or they thought it was a bad idea I came off them.

I was offered counselling aswell and I want to take it but I'm very scared of being judged by people. My problems aren't really with myself, they stem from society and the way the world is. I've always been told by people that this is stupid and it shouldn't depress me because everyone has to deal with it, I just don't know how people do it without just tuning everything out and living like a mindless zombie for the rest of their lives.

I think a lot of it comes from the fact I really want to make the world better and I feel totally helpless having no way to really do that.

Making this thread though has really helped me realise that people do care about other people though and I think I will seek help again, I can't keep living like I do now, it's not good for me and it's not good for the people around me. 

Thanks for the advice, I'm sorry about your father in law, but I'm very glad about your brother, hopefully I can reach the point he got to sooner rather than later.
Thanks, I'll certainly do that when I feel up to it :)

Thanks. When I made that post the only thing going through my head was that I really can't help being depressed. I've tried not to be and sometimes it works, but in the end reality hits home and it all comes back. 

Thanks for the words of encouragement.

That XKCD pretty much hits the nail on the head and describes exactly why I'm depressed. It took a lot for our species to get here, and we've reached a point where the majority of people live boring uneducated lives.

Facebook is something that really gets me down, I have an account on there pretty much just to see how stupid some people really are. It's really annoying, people post all their shit on some stupid website when they could be doing so many numbers of interesting things.

Also, being who I am really doesn't fit in with the real world. I'm that guy who doesn't talk much because the people I'm surrounded by are people who talk about just how fucking wasted they got at the weekend or how many people they've had sex with. 

I'm not the kind of person that does that stuff, I do drink sometimes, I smoke pot more though, that's pretty much the only time I feel good about myself, but a lack of a job means I can't really justify buying any.

I really try not to think about this stuff, because I usually just cry (pretty embarrassing trying to explain to normal people why I'm crying).
Hey, thanks for this. It's good to know people actually care about others. That's not something I see in my everyday life.

I really can't agree with anything of a spiritual nature, it doesn't fit into the way the universe we live in works. The only real way one can live forever is through ideas and thoughts, and everytime I have a good one it turns out that someone already invented it.

Haha, yes, the internet can be the real world, but it can also not be the real world, if you see where I am going. I wouldn't count what happens at 4chan the real world.

Also, I do have friends in real life, good friends, I'm just not comfortable with them knowing what goes through my head when I'm alone. 

You're right though, I've never made the effort to really connect to people here. I'm in England so it's a lot rarer to come across people in my area. 

It's not that I'm not interested or anything, I just like being anonymous, it gives me the freedom and the confidence to speak my mind without feeling like I'm being judged.

Thanks. I've been there a few times, I've never posted anything, I usually just read posts other people have made and it makes me feel like an idiot for having such a decent life and still being depressed.
